title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LORETTA'S LAKE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Loretta Simmons, a mail carrier from Macon, Georgia.
Every Fourth of July, her family swims out to the sandbar at Lake Sinclair.
And for fifty years, Loretta has stayed on the dock, guarding the potato salad.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE DOCK
segments.quote: The very cave you are afraid to enter turns out to be the source of what you are looking for.
segments.author: Joseph Campbell
lines: Her niece asked, Aunt Lo, why don't you ever come out?
That night, she remembered a line from Joseph Campbell, taped in her mail truck:
The very cave you are afraid to enter turns out to be the source of what you are looking for.
Her cave was the lake. Next morning, she signed up for grown-up swim lessons at the Y.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE SWIM CAP
segments.quote: For what do we live, but to make sport for our neighbours, and laugh at them in our turn?
segments.author: Jane Austen
lines: She showed up in a bright green swim cap, looking like a tennis ball.
Her teacher Clarence, a retired Navy diver, pulled on his own orange cap and quoted Jane Austen:
For what do we live, but to make sport for our neighbours, and laugh at them in our turn?
So Loretta laughed first. Then she put her face in the water.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE TOOLBOX
segments.quote: When you swim you don't grab hold of the water, because if you do you will sink and drown. Instead you relax, and float.
segments.author: Alan Watts
lines: Floating was harder. She sank like a toolbox, grabbing the water like it owed her money.
Clarence read her a line from the philosopher Alan Watts:
When you swim you don't grab hold of the water, because if you do you will sink and drown. Instead you relax, and float.
So she let go, lay back, and floated.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE TEST
segments.quote: Keep on beginning and failing. Each time you fail, start all over again, and you will grow stronger.
segments.author: Anne Sullivan
lines: Then came the deep-end test. Halfway, she panicked, grabbed the rope, and failed.
In the parking lot, Clarence showed her a line from Anne Sullivan, Helen Keller's teacher:
Keep on beginning and failing. Each time you fail, start all over again, and you will grow stronger.
So she swam laps before every mail route. Two weeks later, she passed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE SANDBAR
segments.quote: It takes courage for a man to listen to his own goodness and act on it.
segments.author: Pablo Casals
lines: On the Fourth of July, Loretta swam to the sandbar. Her family went crazy.
Then she looked back. Her brother Curtis sat alone on the dock, guarding the potato salad. He can't swim either.
She thought of the cellist Pablo Casals:
It takes courage for a man to listen to his own goodness and act on it.
She swam back, handed Curtis a pool noodle, and said, Your turn.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: SATURDAYS
segments.quote: All that is really worth the doing is what we do for others.
segments.author: Lewis Carroll
lines: Curtis sank like a toolbox too. It runs in the family.
By Labor Day, he reached the sandbar, yelling the whole way.
Clarence quoted Lewis Carroll, from an old letter:
All that is really worth the doing is what we do for others.
Now Loretta and Clarence teach grown-ups every Saturday. Green caps for everyone.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Enter the cave. Laugh first. Let go. Start again. Go back for someone. Pass it on.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Enter the cave. Laugh first. Let go. Start again. Go back for someone.
Me? I float beautifully. It's the steering I never figured out.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
